name: Baranów Sandomierski Castle
architectural_style: A Renaissance castle-palace built by the Leszczyński family around 1591–1606, probably designed by the Italian architect Santi Gucci; remodelled after 1695 for the Lubomirski family by Tylman van Gameren, rebuilt after an 1898 fire by the Dolański family under architect Tadeusz Stryjeński (who added an Art Nouveau chapel with Józef Mehoffer stained glass and a Jacek Malczewski altar painting), and restored again in 1956–1968 after wartime damage; the building's features and room decoration are inspired by Kraków's Wawel Castle, though it is not independently confirmed as a deliberate miniature of it

highlights: Built by the Leszczyński family around 1591–1606 as a Renaissance residence, with the Italian architect Santi Gucci as the probable designer
Remodelled after 1695 for the Lubomirski family by the architect Tylman van Gameren

description:
Baranów Sandomierski Castle stands in the town of the same name in Subcarpathian Voivodeship, south-eastern Poland, a Renaissance castle-palace built by the Leszczyński family around 1591 to 1606. The Italian architect Santi Gucci is thought to be its probable designer, and the building's features and the decoration of its halls draw recognisable inspiration from Kraków's Wawel Castle — a connection confirmed by those architectural and decorative details rather than any documented claim that Baranów was built as a deliberate miniature of Wawel.

Ownership and architecture both shifted after 1695, when the Lubomirski family had the castle remodelled by Tylman van Gameren, one of the leading architects working in Poland at the time. A fire in 1898 caused heavy damage, and the rebuilding that followed, carried out by the Dolański family under the architect Tadeusz Stryjeński, added one of the castle's most distinctive features: an Art Nouveau chapel with stained glass by Józef Mehoffer and an altar painting by Jacek Malczewski, two of the leading Polish artists of the period. The castle was damaged again during the Second World War and restored between 1956 and 1968.

Today the castle combines a museum — including a portrait room of Polish kings and a stucco gallery attributed to Tylman van Gameren — with a hotel. A handful of rooms and suites sit inside the castle itself, including royal-style bedchambers, while most guest accommodation is in a separate hotel building next to the castle, within the surrounding park of about 14 hectares. Sources disagree on the exact total room count, so no single figure is given here.
history: Built by the Leszczyński family around 1591–1606 as a Renaissance residence, with the Italian architect Santi Gucci as the probable designer. After 1695 the Lubomirski family had it remodelled with the architect Tylman van Gameren. It was heavily damaged by a fire in 1898 and rebuilt by the Dolański family under the architect Tadeusz Stryjeński, who added an Art Nouveau chapel with stained glass by Józef Mehoffer and an altar painting by Jacek Malczewski. After damage in the Second World War it was restored in 1956–1968.

faqs.question: Is Baranów Sandomierski Castle really a 'little Wawel'?
faqs.answer: The castle is often described that way, but this isn't an independently confirmed claim — what's established is that certain architectural features and the decoration of its rooms were inspired by Kraków's Wawel Castle, not that Baranów was deliberately built as a scaled-down replica.

faqs.question: Can I stay inside the castle itself at Baranów Sandomierski?
faqs.answer: A handful of rooms and suites, including royal-style bedchambers, are inside the castle itself, but most guest accommodation is in a separate hotel building next to the castle, within the surrounding park. Specify which building you want when booking.

faqs.question: Who added the Art Nouveau chapel at Baranów Sandomierski Castle?
faqs.answer: It was added during the rebuilding that followed an 1898 fire, carried out by the Dolański family under the architect Tadeusz Stryjeński, with stained glass by Józef Mehoffer and an altar painting by Jacek Malczewski.

hotel.how_to_stay:
**Getting there:** In Baranów Sandomierski in south-eastern Poland, with the castle set in a park of about 14 hectares; parking is available at the property (confirm when booking).

**Rooms & rates:** From approx. €113/night. The cheapest rooms are in Hotel Zamkowy, a building next to the castle; other rooms (for example a 20 m² double with an inner-courtyard view from approx. €125) are listed separately, so check which building each room is in when you book.

**On-site:** Breakfast is included, along with one hour of spa a day in the rates seen on Booking; the Magnacka restaurant serves traditional Polish cuisine, and the castle also houses a museum.

**Good to know:** Specify castle or hotel building when you book, as the two feel different. The castle is also a museum, so rooms and exhibitions share the building.

**Combine with:** The castle museum (portrait room of Polish kings and the stucco gallery of Tylman van Gameren) and its park.
